description: We are a team passionate about space exploration, science, and technology. We combine software development, problem-solving, and creative thinking to transform open NASA data into meaningful solutions. For this challenge, we aim to identify and analyze Earth environments that resemble the Moon and Mars, using technology and scientific research to support future space exploration. We welcome people with skills in programming, data analysis, GIS, geology, and planetary science.
summary: ATLANIA is an open-science planetary observatory and interactive 3D atlas designed to identify and evaluate terrestrial analog environments on Earth for Moon and Mars exploration. Connecting 35 terrestrial sites with 6 planetary targets, it calculates a transparent 5-axis Analog Suitability Index (ASI)—Geomorphology, Aridity, Thermal, Radiation, and Logistics—powered by NASA POWER, NASA GIBS, and ESA Copernicus DEM GLO-90 data. Researchers can compare dual 3D terrains side-by-side (such as the Galápagos volcanic shields against Mare Tranquillitatis), probe real-time coordinates, and export standardized mission dossiers.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Selecting terrestrial testbeds for lunar and Martian hardware, EVA protocols, and astrobiology instruments typically relies on fragmented literature and static PDFs. ATLANIA replaces qualitative guesswork with a reproducible 5-axis Analog Suitability Index (ASI) across 35 terrestrial sites and 6 extraterrestrial targets (Moon and Mars).

1. Planetary Observatory: An interactive 3D celestial-geological interface mapping crust, mantle, and core contexts alongside orbital analogs.

2. Terra Explorer (2D/3D Split-Screen): Powered by MapLibre GL JS and NASA/ESA layers, featuring an interactive 5-axis radar chart (Geomorphology, Aridity, Thermal Regime, UV/Solar Radiation, and Logistical Accessibility) with customizable mission-weight sliders.

3. HD 3D Topographic Twin: A dual-viewport Three.js/WebGL diorama rendering real elevation meshes from ESA Copernicus DEM GLO-90, comparing sites like the Galápagos volcanic basalt shields (Ecuador) directly against Mare Tranquillitatis (Moon) or Olympus Mons (Mars).

4. Live Coordinate Probing & Mission Dossier Export: Click any coordinate on Earth to query real-time NASA POWER climatology and Copernicus elevation data, compute its live ASI score, and export a standardized Markdown/JSON scientific dossier.

Benefits & Intended Impact

ATLANIA democratizes planetary mission planning for space agencies, university researchers, and rover engineering teams, highlighting high-value Latin American analogs (such as the Galápagos Islands and Atacama) alongside global benchmarks.

Tools, Coding Languages & Stack

- Frontend & 3D Engine: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js / React Three Fiber, MapLibre GL JS.

- Data & Scientific Pipeline: Python, FastAPI, NumPy, SciPy (hypsometric curves, topographic ruggedness, and 5-axis ASI normalization).

Super Intelligence (SI) / AI Transparency Disclosure

- Code & Architecture: AI coding assistants (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, and Gemini) were used to assist in scaffolding Next.js UI components, MapLibre/Three.js shaders, and Python data normalization scripts. All scientific formulas, weightings, and architecture were designed and verified by Team Vyntra.

- Demo Video & Voiceover: The 30-second demo video voiceover was synthesized using Microsoft Edge Neural TTS (edge-tts, en-US-AndrewNeural) from a script written by Team Vyntra, and the video scenes were assembled at 60fps using Remotion.
